title: Dabur India Ltd - 500096 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Dabur Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 7.3% YoY with India FMCG up 9.5% on 6% volume; FY27 guidance raised to high-single to low-double-digit growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 7.3% YoY in Q4 FY26, with domestic FMCG up 9.5% on 6% volume growth and HPC up 17%. Operating profit rose 8.2% and reported PAT rose 15%. International grew a muted 2.5% in INR terms, with the Middle East hit by the West Asia war. Management raised FY27 revenue guidance to high-single to low-double-digit growth, citing price increases to offset roughly 10% input inflation, and said India margins would be protected.

financial_highlights.change: rural outpacing urban by about 300 bps

segments.name: Hair Care (Hair Oils)
segments.commentary: Hair oil grew 28% YoY, with price up about 9% and volume about 14%; market share gain of 154 bps. Coconut portfolio grew 48%, Almond 57%.

segments.name: Hair Care (Shampoos)
segments.commentary: Shampoo grew 20%; bottle saliency about 22% and rising as sachet mix shifts toward bottles.

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: Home Care grew 24%. Odonil up 20% with 243 bps share gain; Odomos up 48% with 88 bps gain; Sanifresh over 20%.

segments.name: Oral Care
segments.commentary: Toothpaste grew 7.2% in Q4 vs category about 2.5%; Meswak about 11%, herbal toothpaste 30-40%, Dabur Red 6-7%, Babool 1-2%. FY oral care growth about 9-10%.

segments.name: Skin Care
segments.commentary: Skin care grew about 12.5%, driven by Gulabari and OxyLife.

segments.name: Health Care - Digestives
segments.commentary: Digestives grew mid-teens; Hajmola up 12.7% with 233 bps share gain, Isabgol up over 50%.

segments.name: Health Care - Glucose
segments.commentary: Glucose declined about 24-25% in Q4, hit by unseasonal March rains; it is about 20-25% of Q4 health care sales.

segments.name: Health Care - OTC/Ethical
segments.commentary: OTC and Ethical grew high single digits; Honitus up 36%, Ayurvedic health juices up 30%, Lal Tail up 10%. Honey grew over 20% in Q4 and about 18% for the full year.

segments.name: Beverages
segments.commentary: Sequential recovery in Q4. Real Activ juices grew 26%, Coconut Water 100%, with 250 bps share gain in Nectars and 280 bps in Activ. Management targets mid-to-high single-digit growth in beverages for Q1.

segments.name: Culinary
segments.commentary: Culinary grew 30%, led by Fats and Oils and Hommade; Badshah grew 12%.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Muted 2.5% INR growth. Sub-Saharan Africa up 20%, UK and EU up 10%, Hobi up 16.5%, Bangladesh up 22%, Namaste US up 6.2%. Middle East (about 30-35% of international) impacted.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance revised up to high-single to low-double-digit, from earlier high-single-digit, with about half from volume and the rest from price.
HPC expected to grow at least double digit in FY27, possibly high teens.
Q1 FY27 growth expected to sustain; April showed good HPC traction; sequential improvement expected.
Margins expected to improve sequentially in Q1 and year-on-year for FY27, with India margins protected through a 4% price increase and a second round of pricing considered.
International expected to grow in double digits over time, though volume and pricing will fall in the Middle East; rupee depreciation of about 6% gives translation benefit.
capex_capacity: Coconut water: an AFET line is in place with surplus capacity; management said capacity is being augmented as it goes.
Coconut water ARR is about INR100 crore, with exit rate targeted at INR150 crore; longer-term aspiration INR200 crore.
New premium hair oil launches (post-bath and hair nourishment) planned for Q1-Q2 FY27.
Nectar: new PET bottles and INR50 and INR100 price points introduced; sugar reduction planned.
Alternative supply routes for international being set up from India, Egypt and Turkey after disruption at Ras Al Khaimah.
demand_pricing: Rural GT and total FMCG: Nielsen FMCG growth about 9.2% (rural 11.4%, urban 8%); the urban-rural gap narrowed from about 500 bps to about 340 bps.
Inflation on RM/PM now about 10% across most HPC portfolios, barring beverages and healthcare; budget had assumed flat inflation.
4% price increases announced across HPC; shrinkflation applied to INR10 and INR20 packs; GST cut helped about 70% of portfolio on higher tax rate.
Quick commerce about 75% of e-commerce salience (up from 50% in Q3), with growth around 50%.
Crude-linked raw materials about 25% of RM; packaging about one-third of RM basket; LUPs about 30% of business.
Oral care category growing about 2.5% and herbal toothpaste about 6%, against non-herbal about 2.8%; management says market leader may recover on low base.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a one-off in the strong 20-36% growth, and will Q1 growth sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 growth will sustain, with HPC traction in April. Beverages are expected to grow mid-to-high single digit, and glucose and summer portfolios are expected to grow double digit if summer is severe.

qa_highlights.question: Are you satisfied with toothpaste performance, and is the market leader recovering?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is unhappy with oral care at 6-7% in Q4, with full-year oral care at about 9-10%. Management expects a strong double-digit Q1 led by Dabur Red, Meswak and Herbal, and said Babool is growing only 1-2%.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 margins expand given crude-led inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 margins are visible for India business and will sequentially improve; the target is year-on-year improvement via pricing, mix, premiumisation and cost savings. International margins are less certain if the war persists.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the HPC growth and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Hair oil growth was 28%, with price about 9% and volume about 14%, driven by perfumed oils as coconut prices rose. Management said HPC should grow at least double digit next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Chyawanprash decline and how is glucose impacting health care?
qa_highlights.answer: Chyawanprash is seasonal and low in Q4, so it is inconsequential. Glucose is about 20-25% of Q4 health care and fell 24-25%, while the rest of health care grew about 12.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How much did GST cuts help, and what is the international impact?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of the portfolio was on higher GST, with hair oil, shampoo and oral care growth attributed to GST relief. Middle East (30-35% of international) faces supply chain, inflation and demand hits; alternative routes are being set up at higher cost.

risks_watch: West Asia war driving about 10% input inflation and supply disruption; second round of price increases depends on the war's trajectory.
Middle East business (about 30-35% of international) hit by supply chain, inflation and expat demand declines; international margin pressure if war persists.
El Nino and monsoon risk to glucose, beverages and rural demand; Nielsen FMCG growth slowed from 11% to 9%.
Price-led growth may reduce volume; management acknowledged it may cede some share if competitors do not take price.
Oral care growth at 6-7% in Q4 and Babool at 1-2%; market leader may recover share.
Advertising spend may be cut in favour of margin protection if inflation remains high.
summary.management_tone: Confident on HPC momentum and the price-led recovery, but openly unhappy with oral care and cautious on the Middle East and the duration of the war. Management kept the India margin commitment firm while leaving international margin outcome unresolved.
key_quotes: We are quite unhappy with this performance because entire HPC portfolio has grown by 17% with oral care being a outlier where we've seen a muted performance of around 6%, 7% growth in Oral Care.
So, we will prioritize our margin over our media spend going forward.
Even if we have to take a little bit cut in terms of shares, we are okay with it.
We now see an inflation of roughly around 10% hitting us in a lot of portfolios, barring the portfolio of beverages and healthcare.

adds.what: Coconut water AFET line in place with surplus capacity; capacity being augmented as it goes
New premium hair oil launches (post-bath and hair nourishment)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance raised to high-single to low-double-digit (midpoint ~10%), about half volume and half price, backed by a 4% HPC price increase and share gains in hair oil, home care and oral care; no new capacity or order book quantified, so backing is partial.
